pr_title: feat: implement prompt for remote renaming
pr_body:
fixes #847 

Changes:
A prompt asking for the name of fork remote, if there is already remote with same name, another prompt asking for name of source remote to rename it, otherwise just add the remote name from the first prompt.

Behaviour if the entered name of remote is already a remote name:
![remote-renaming](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40687700/93760504-c3f9ad00-fc29-11ea-9b05-849e5c10adf5.gif)

Behaviour if the entered name of remote is not a remote name:
![remote-renaming-2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40687700/93760525-cc51e800-fc29-11ea-8915-aff4bc0b6100.gif)
pr_comments: I think this is a nice direction but would rather @mislav and @ampinsk weigh in.

As I mentioned in issue #847, I didn't learn Go yet! The offline fork I had is mostly based on the previous implementations.
So I don't know how to fix the tests! If someone can give guidance on how to fix, I will try to fix them!

I came here looking for an issue to add an optional name to the fork itself, not only the remote name – for example, when several repos have the same name, but within different user or org workspaces. Don't want to derail this PR, just checking to see if there's some common use cases here. A few other things that feel related:
- recent changes: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/1706
- similar need, different workflow: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/1399

i'll see this through. TODO:

- [x] add option for accepting remote name
- [x] in case of conflict, error and tell to use remote name flag
- [x] tests

So this is changing the previous behavior, right? If you cloned a repo from origin, then added a fork, you would have the old origin be added to the `upstream` remote, and the new `origin` would be your fork. As I understand, this isn't possible anymore:

https://asciinema.org/a/DRebWnUq73hVcNAY8lZdVXolV

As much as I like having the option to pass a name, this is marked as an addition, but it's also a feature removal, and it'll be missed :c
Is a compromise here a `--rename` flag that restores and opts into the old behavior?

In my opinion a flag would not resolve it.
if i simply run `gh repo fork` I would prefer it assumed if something is named `origin` it should rename it to `upstream` as in the previous behavior.
now if you run `gh repo fork --remote-name` than no renaming needs to happen so why add the `rename` flag?

Perhaps `rename` flag could be added if the remote found was unexpected as in not `origin`
Maybe I am different as I preferred the magic instead of being prompted and I also prefer not to have to remember each incantation of flags.

If anything though `gh repo fork` still lacks the ability to rename the `repo` before forking it which is a bigger issue than what your `remote` is called locally but I digress.
Fine `--rename` would work, I'll just end up wrapping the command 😅

issue_context.title: Unwanted remote naming after gh repo fork
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

gh version 0.7.0 (2020-04-22)

`gh repo fork` renames `origin` to `upstream` and sets my fork as `origin`. I want to retain `origin` untouched and add an origin named `fork`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

I had a clone of an organization repo

```console
$ git remote -v
origin	ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git (fetch)
origin	ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git (push)
```

I forked it

```console
$ gh repo fork
- Forking org/repo...
✓ Created fork jglick/repo
? Would you like to add a remote for the fork? Yes
✓ Renamed origin remote to upstream
✓ Added remote origin
$ git remote -v
origin	git@github.com:jglick/repo.git (fetch)
origin	git@github.com:jglick/repo.git (push)
upstream	ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git (fetch)
upstream	ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git (push)
```

### Expected vs actual behavior

I wanted to see

```console
$ gh repo fork
- Forking org/repo...
✓ Created fork jglick/repo
? Would you like to add a remote for the fork? Yes
✓ Added remote fork
$ git remote -v
fork	git@github.com:jglick/repo.git (fetch)
fork	git@github.com:jglick/repo.git (push)
origin	ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git (fetch)
origin	ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git (push)
```

or be prompted.

### Workaround

```bash
git remote rename origin fork
git remote rename upstream origin
```
comments:
Can we introduce a flag for asking the remote name for the fork?
If the user specifies the remote name, well and good.  
If not:
1. If the 'origin' remote already exists, show an error and suggest using the flag.
2. If the 'origin' remote does not exist, set that.

For context and discussion leading to the current behavior, see #582 (/cc @cben).

I do agree that renaming the remotes is undesirable, but I think the main problem here is that the user is not told about the upcoming renaming in advance.

So instead of being told of the renaming only after the fact, as is the current behavior:

```console
$ gh repo fork
- Forking someorg/foobar...
✓ Created fork myusername/foobar
? Would you like to add a remote for the fork? Yes
✓ Renamed origin remote to upstream
✓ Added remote origin
```

...I'd like to _at least_ be informed of the impending rename; something like:

```console
$ gh repo fork
- Forking someorg/foobar...
✓ Created fork myusername/foobar
? Would you like to add a remote for the fork? Yes
? Would you like to rename the current 'origin' remote to 'upstream'? Yes
✓ Renamed origin remote to upstream
✓ Added remote origin
```

...with the following alternative outcome, should I pick "no" in the second prompt:

```console
$ gh repo fork
- Forking someorg/foobar...
✓ Created fork myusername/foobar
? Would you like to add a remote for the fork? Yes
? Would you like to rename the current 'origin' remote to 'upstream'? No
✓ Added remote fork # Or myusername
```

Can we please have a config option to control this behaviour. 

I want the behaviour I currently have with `hub fork`, i.e. it leaves origin unchanged and adds the remote using the name of the organization/user that the fork was created in

Aside: Ha! Just noticed the issue creator is a fellow ☁️ 🐝 

🤣

Nicer workaround:

```bash
gh alias set --shell fork2 'git remote -v && gh repo fork --remote && git remote rename origin fork && git remote rename upstream origin && git remote -v'
```

Use as:

```bash
gh fork2
```
I was using a offline fork with aforementioned feature with a prompt for sometime. If it's okay can I open a PR?

@dfireBird Sure, I'd like us to address this is the next feature release! A PR that adds a prompt would be welcome. I'm also thinking that something like a `--remote-name` flag for automation would also be great.
I don't know go yet! So I just copied and pasted previous code from the repository for the prompt and I had some itty hack I did! I will make sure to correct it and open a PR.

@vilmibm thanks for adopting and merging #1882! It's definitely a large step in the right direction, but I actually find the UX implemented there a little cumbersome (requiring the user to repeat the command, this time passing the `--remote-name="fork"`):

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/105253590-a33c5800-5b34-11eb-932f-f0e18bf08e2d.png)

Couldn't the first invocation offer the option to provide the fork name interactively, like this?

- Scenario where the user accepts renaming origin to upstream:
  ```console
  $ gh repo fork
  - Forking someorg/foobar...
  ✓ Created fork myusername/foobar
  ? Would you like to add a remote for the fork? Yes
  ! A remote called 'origin' already exists
  ? Would you like to rename the current 'origin' remote to 'upstream'? Yes
  ✓ Renamed 'origin' remote to 'upstream'
  ✓ Added remote 'origin'
  ```

- Scenario where the user rejects renaming origin to upstream (same sequence except for the last 3 lines):
  ```console
  $ gh repo fork
  - Forking someorg/foobar...
  ✓ Created fork myusername/foobar
  ? Would you like to add a remote for the fork? Yes
  ! A remote called 'origin' already exists
  ? Would you like to rename the current 'origin' remote to 'upstream'? No
  ? What should be the remote name for the fork? fork
  ✓ Added remote 'fork'
  ```

Is this something that could be tracked in a separate issue, or are you against that kind of behavior in principle?

I actually like it being a flag, because now I can
```
alias fork='gh repo fork --remote --remote-name=cben'
```
and not deal with any prompts. :heart:

Sure, I am not advocating for removal of the flag :) In fact, I will probably also do something similar to your alias, since I'm used to that workflow thanks to `hub` :) but for people who don't yet have strong preferences, the default experience could be more ergonomic. In other words, we could have both a flag and interactive prompts if the flag isn't passed, rather than an error requesting to run the command again.

(On a related note, it might be a good idea to allow configuring a default remote name for forks via [gh config](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_config), so that one doesn't have to override the default `fork` subcommand with an alias.)

@waldyrious thanks for the feedback! In general we're trying to find the correct balance of prompting + magic + maintainability. We felt that implicit renaming was too much magic but more prompting == more difficult tests and less maintainable code. It's possible we'll want prompts back, here, but for now wanted to err on the side of simpler code.

I'll say that while friendly prompts and a major goal of `gh` we are trying to be more careful with them until we have a better framework for testing them and, possibly, new primitives for prompts that we're more comfortable maintaining.

Thanks for the response. I'll be looking forward to improved maintainability of prompt-based code, as those are one of the key aspects that make `gh` work so well IMO, and would definitely improve this flow, in particular.

After #2982 revised my workaround https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/847#issuecomment-689049145 to be similar to https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/847#issuecomment-764745730:

```bash
gh alias set fork 'repo fork --remote --remote-name fork'
```

review_comments:
This clearly broke existing functionality to rename existing remote to `upstream` 😭
The pattern of origin, upstream is very common when forking due to scripts and muscle memory.
